🚨HORRIBLE: Sewage has mixed with rainwater as floodwaters engulf displaced Palestinians’ tents in Gaza. For the fourth consecutive winter, families are once again facing flooding, contamination, and unimaginable suffering as a result of Israel’s genocidal war.

Why is Gaza drowning? Images of floods engulfing Gaza have gone viral. Most coverage focuses on the humanitarian catastrophe. Few explain what caused it. Since October 2023, Israeli forces have destroyed nearly all of Gaza’s infrastructure. Up to 68 million tons of rubble now blanket the Strip. Homes, schools, hospitals, and basic services have been flattened, with at least 90 percent of the territory destroyed. Now, as winter sets in, the first rains are making what is left unlivable. At least five people have been killed after sand embankments collapsed in the downpour. None of this is new. The Israeli plan to make Gaza unlivable has been unfolding for years. In 2012, the UN warned that Gaza could be unlivable by 2020 because of repeated Israeli assaults, a crippling blockade, the collapse of its aquifer, energy shortages, and mass unemployment. Despite the so-called ceasefire, our reporter in Gaza describes a situation that is impossible to endure: no shelter, no aid, and a ban on rebuilding. Conditions are getting worse by the day.” @specter_affairs

Israeli forces demolished the homes of two Palestinian prisoners as Al Jazeera’s Nida Ibrahim was reporting on Israel’s collective punishment campaign across the occupied West Bank. Now the families of these prisoners are homeless and not allowed to rebuild.

This year’s olive harvest has been the most violent in recent memory, with settler attacks on Palestinian farmers reaching a new high. But for Masafer Yatta, this is only the latest escalation in a decades-long campaign by the Israeli state to expel Palestinians from their land by any means necessary. Working in coordination with the army and police, nearby settlers wage a ceaseless battle against the Palestinians living in this area. Professor Ilan Pappé describes what has been happening to Masafer Yatta since the 1970’s as “incremental colonization, ethnic cleansing, and oppression,” and to be here is to see it firsthand. But the people of Masafer Yatta have earned a reputation for themselves for their resistance to state and settler terror. They simply refuse to leave, and the Israelis simply won’t stop trying to force them to. The Nakba never ended. We’re just watching its latest act.

Some lands are known for their beauty, others for their history. But Palestine carries a story that stretches far beyond its borders, a story written in ancient streets, olive trees and generations of people who call it home. This is Palestine! Welcome to Palestine! 🇵🇸❤️ Located in the Middle East, Palestine consists of two territories: the West Bank and the Gaza Strip, along the eastern Mediterranean. In Bethlehem, the birthplace of Jesus, the ancient Church of the Nativity stands as one of Christianity's most important historic sites. Then there's Jericho, one of the world's oldest continuously inhabited cities, where thousands of years of human history can still be felt. In Nablus, traditional markets, historic architecture and the famous Palestinian knafeh reveal a culture rich in flavour and tradition. And in Battir, ancient stone terraces, olive groves and beautiful landscapes tell the story of generations connected to the land. But Palestine is more than ancient buildings and beautiful scenery. It is a place of deep cultural traditions, distinctive embroidery, traditional music, delicious food and remarkable hospitality. From its historic cities to its Mediterranean coastline, Palestine carries a heritage that deserves to be discovered and remembered. So, if you could experience one place in Palestine, where would you go? Drop the Palestinian flag in the comments, and follow Travel Scope for more incredible stories from around the world! #Palestine #FreePalestine #Gaza #VisitPalestine #PalestinianCulture

For 18 months, a group of journalists from the Palestine Reporting Lab, Lighthouse Reports, and ARIJ documented every Israeli roadblock, checkpoint, and barrier that prohibits Palestinian movement across the West Bank. Israeli military checkpoints are one of the biggest obstacles to Palestinian movement. These checkpoints are manned by armed Israeli soldiers, who stop Palestinians as they try to move from town to town, separating Palestinians and often keeping them stuck for hours. Checkpoints are often the site of violence, where armed Israeli soldiers routinely harass, humiliate, beat, and even shoot and kill Palestinians as they attempt to cross. The journalists found that Palestinians lose at least 90 minutes a week looking for new routes around the checkpoints so they do not have to risk their lives crossing them. Check out their reports documenting their findings and interactive map, and their article featured in Wired. Link in bio.
